speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked	the Prime Minister given SGX's challenges in recent years relating to the quantity and quality of listings, turnover, technical disruptions, risk management, including a half-day disruption on 14 July 2016 (a) whether the Government is optimistic that SGX's performance and reputation can be revived; (b) what role it sees for SGX in broader economic development; and (c) what steps it is taking to work with the SGX management to catalyse the desired outcomes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Some of them are not unique to SGX or Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: A weak economic outlook and heightened market volatility have been cited as reasons for this lacklustre IPO activity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: While its derivatives business remains among the most dynamic in Asia, its cash equity business has lost some ground to competitors.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX has embarked on several initiatives to strengthen and develop the stock market, with the support of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: A key priority of SGX is to raise the quality of listings.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: A minimum trading price was introduced to address risks associated with low-priced securities and to improve overall market quality.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Three independent Listing Committees were established last year to strengthen the process for admitting new listings and enforcing against listing rule breaches.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX is also adapting to competition from alternative private financing markets.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Recently, it partnered Clearbridge Accelerator, one of Singapore's leading venture capital and incubation firms, to set up Capbridge, a securities-based crowdfunding platform.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Capbridge may also contribute to SGX's IPO pipeline by incubating and providing last-mile funding to high-tech companies before the IPO stage.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It will take time for SGX's initiatives to bear fruit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: A second area that needs improvement is the management of technology and operational risks.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It is not uncommon for exchanges to experience trading disruptions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: System failures and trading halts have occurred in several major exchanges in recent years.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: But SGX needs to do better in reducing the frequency of these disruptions and in managing any disruptions well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS is closely supervising SGX's progress in enhancing the resilience of its systems Page: 40 and recovery processes and in engaging stakeholders effectively.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Thirdly, SGX is creating new business opportunities, by building on its strengths.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For example, it has the largest listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REIT) and Business Trusts sector in Asia, excluding Japan, and continues to attract such listings from local and foreign sponsors.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX plans to launch its first exchange-traded fund for Singapore REITs in the later part of this year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX is also a leading player in the Asian time zone in equity derivatives and advancing further.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It expanded its Nifty suite of futures contracts in June this year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The exchange is growing its capabilities in foreign exchange (FX) derivatives and is collaborating with a leading electronic trading platform in FX to offer block FX futures in the later part of this year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It is building on its existing strengths, staying nimble to new opportunities and working to improve its system resilience.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier in his answer, he mentioned that MAS is closely supervising SGX's efforts to build information technology (IT) resilience.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My second question is, notwithstanding what the Acting Minister said about falling trading volumes worldwide, it was reported that from 2011 to 2015, the value of shares traded per day on SGX had fallen by a third over these last four years.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My third question is that I understand that some Singapore companies are choosing not to list themselves locally but are going to regional bourses to list.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Has SGX or even the Government looked into the reasons why they do not find listing in Singapore attractive?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On IT resilience, I would say that it is totally in SGX's interest to make sure that it performs well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are no agency issues here, where the interests of MAS or the economy or the Government are different from SGX's.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Therefore, it is totally in their interest to make sure that it performs well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think it was last week that they had started a new industry working group.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This will engage all industry experts and stakeholders as a working group to seriously look into these issues.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They will study all the responses that are needed to make sure that if and when such disruptions happen again, SGX can respond more effectively and in a more timely manner to minimise the disruption.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Let us wait for the work of the industry working group.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the other two questions, I would perhaps answer them together.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One is the fall in the trading volume from 2011 to 2015.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is source for concern because it is also a global phenomenon.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the one hand, we also recognise that SGX and IPO activity might have come down, but on the other hand, financing activities are coming up globally.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For example, angel investment funds, Page: 41 private equity funds, REITs – all these continue to do very well, including crowdfunding.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Notwithstanding the fact that one area of the financial sector maybe facing lacklustre performance, overall, the financial sector can actually continue to do well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The analogy is not very different from let us say, taxis.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the one hand, traditional cabs may be feeling the squeeze but, on the other hand, commuters are benefiting from other options of commuting such as Uber and Grab.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is what we are seeing, too, in the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Innovation is coming on board; we are seeing different kinds of financing options, and these will still serve the Singapore market and Singapore economy fairly well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If you look at specific clusters or counters, such as technology or healthcare stocks, we are actually performing well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: All in all, jobs are also at stake here.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will do our best to prop up this sector as well as we can.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If anyone requires skills upgrading, we have the Institute of Banking and Finance, so those in the financial sector can continue to upgrade their skills so that the sector will continue to do well.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In the past, when the first two glitches happened in 2014, there were very strong statements made by Government leaders, in fact, saying that this is unacceptable coming from SGX.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Or what are the levers available to MAS?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On Singapore companies listing overseas, I think this will have to be left as their business strategy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some Singapore companies list on regional bourses maybe because their businesses are there.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What we need to do is make sure that our stock exchange is also competitive, so that foreign companies can also list here.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have to position ourselves as part of the landscape so that it is not very different from other businesses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As I mentioned earlier, the industry working group will come up with their recommendations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Let us look at what they come up with, what are the steps.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Unfortunately, around the region and the world, technical disruptions do happen from time to time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We want to make sure that when it happens, if it ever happens, we will respond to it Page: 42 as fast as we can.
